US-119-HJRES218.title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to abolish the electoral college and to provide for the direct election of the President and Vice President of the United States.

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in House

US-119-HJRES218.aiSummary: The resolution would change the Constitution to end the electoral college and have the President and Vice President chosen by direct vote. People in the states and the District of Columbia would each cast one vote for a pair of candidates. The pair with the most votes would win, and the change would take effect one year after the first day of January following ratification.

US-119-HR10291.title: JARED Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10291.description: To require a background investigation and certain disclosures from covered persons representing the Federal Government before a foreign sovereign, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10291.aiSummary: The bill would require certain people who represent the federal government before a foreign government to pass a background check before getting access to classified information. They would also have to file yearly financial disclosure forms and could not take deals that directly benefit them from a foreign government they dealt with for the United States. The Office of Government Ethics would report these filings and any violations to Congress and the public each quarter, and people who break the rules could face removal, loss of clearance, or criminal penalties.

US-119-SJRES80.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management relating to "National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska Integrated Activity Plan Record of Decision".
US-119-SJRES80.summary:
This joint resolution reopens portions of the National Petroleum Reserve for oil and gas leasing. (The reserve is an approximately 23-million-acre area on Alaska’s North Slope.)

Specifically, the joint resolution nullifies a plan submitted by the Bureau of Land Management in a rule titled National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska Integrated Activity Plan Record of Decision and issued on April 25, 2022. The 2022 plan replaced the 2020 plan and closed approximately 48% of the reserve to oil and gas leasing in order to protect certain surface resources and uses, such as protecting wildlife and providing subsistence for communities. Thus, the joint resolution removes the protections provided under the 2022 plan and reverts to the 2020 plan.

US-119-HJRES25.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Internal Revenue Service relating to "Gross Proceeds Reporting by Brokers That Regularly Provide Services Effectuating Digital Asset Sales".
US-119-HJRES25.summary:
This joint resolution nullifies requirements for persons effectuating decentralized financial (DeFi) transactions to report certain information regarding digital asset sales to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). Specifically, the joint resolution nullifies the requirements included in the rule titled Gross Proceeds Reporting by Brokers That Regularly Provide Services Effectuating Digital Asset Sales and issued by the IRS on December 30, 2024.

Decentralized finance refers to the suite of financial activities and services that are facilitated by cryptocurrency and intended to be conducted without any sort of reliance on traditional financial tools or intermediaries.
